title: Where did the coupon discount go?
objective: Follow one checkout through this small cart project and discover why reloading a saved cart keeps the coupon label but loses the discount.

snippets.why: The checkout command: build the cart, apply the coupon, print totals and the saved state.
Coupon rules: fixed amount or percent with a cap, clamped to the subtotal.
Only items and the coupon code are persisted; totals are never stored.
The reload path: totals are recalculated from the saved items. The stored coupon code is kept on the cart, but it is never re-applied.
recompute rebuilds every total from the items list and resets the discount to 0. Callers are expected to re-apply coupons after changing items.

nodes.label: checkout command builds the cart and applies the coupon
nodes.note: With a keyboard ($30 x1) and a cable ($12.50 x2), the recorded run prints subtotal 55, discount 5.5, total 49.5.

nodes.label: applyCoupon computes the discount from the coupon rules
nodes.note: TENPCT is 10% off, capped at $20. For subtotal 55 that is 5.5, under the cap.

nodes.label: serialize persists only the items and the coupon code
nodes.note: The recorded checkout output shows the saved state: items plus coupon, with no totals inside.

nodes.label: reload restores the items and recalculates every total
nodes.note: The recorded reload keeps coupon "TENPCT" on the cart but prints discount 0 and total 55.

nodes.label: recompute resets the discount to 0 while recalculating
nodes.note: reload() calls recompute(cart) and never re-applies the stored coupon, so the discount is gone after a reload even though the coupon label survives.

challenges.prompt: You run the checkout command with this input. What will totals.total be in the printed output?
hints: First compute the subtotal from the items: 30 + (12.50 x 2).
TENPCT is 10% off, capped at $20. Compare 10% of the subtotal against the cap.
challenges.explanation: The subtotal is 30 + 25 = 55. TENPCT takes min(10% of 55, cap 20) = 5.5, so total = 55 - 5.5 = 49.5. The recorded run printed exactly {"subtotal":55,"discount":5.5,"total":49.5}.

challenges.prompt: After a reload, the cart still reports coupon "TENPCT" but totals.discount is 0. Which step makes the discount 0?

options.text: recompute recalculating all totals from the items
serialize dropping the totals from the saved state
the reload branch printing the wrong totals

hints: The saved state has no totals at all, so the reload cannot just read them back.
Open step 5 (recompute) and look at what it writes into cart.totals.discount.
challenges.explanation: serialize keeps only items and the coupon code, so reload must rebuild totals. It calls recompute(cart), which sets totals.discount = 0 and totals.total = subtotal. The recorded reload run confirms the result: coupon "TENPCT" with discount 0 and total 55.

challenges.prompt: Where is the actual fault that loses the discount on reload?

options.text: store.js reload(): it recalculates totals but never re-applies the stored coupon
cart.js recompute(): resetting the discount to 0 is itself the bug
pricing.js applyCoupon(): it computes the wrong discount
index.js: the reload branch prints totals incorrectly

hints: The checkout run proves applyCoupon and printing are fine: totals.total was 49.5 before saving.
recompute's reset is a documented contract: callers re-apply coupons after changing items. Which caller fails to do that?
challenges.explanation: The recorded runs narrow it down: checkout prints a correct discounted total, so pricing and printing work; after reload the coupon code is still on the cart but the discount is 0. reload() in store.js rebuilds totals via recompute() and never re-applies the stored coupon. Fixing it means re-applying the coupon inside reload (or persisting the applied discount), not changing recompute's contract.

limitations: This lesson runs against the synthetic cart fixture shipped with the project, not real user code.
No git revision is recorded for the fixture; each file is pinned by its sha256 content hash in sourceSnapshot instead.
Execution evidence covers the checkout and reload commands only; other code paths in the fixture were not run.
